ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In a square grid, the position of $\triangle ABC$ is shown as in the figure, where points A, B, and C are all on the grid points. What is the value of $\cos B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw AD $\perp$ BC and extend BC to meet point D,\\
$\because$ AD=BD=4, $\angle$ADB=90$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ABD is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$B=45$^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\cos B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC on grid paper, with all three vertices on grid points. Point B is at the lower-left grid point, point C is at the grid point to the right on the same horizontal grid line as B, and point A is at the upper-right grid point. Segment BC is horizontal, and A is located to the upper right of B. If a perpendicular is drawn from A to the horizontal line on which BC lies, and the foot of the perpendicular is denoted D, then D is to the right of C, and AD is in the vertical direction, while BD is in the horizontal direction. Counting the grid squares, AD is 4 grid units, and BD is also 4 grid units. Reasoning: Since AD is perpendicular to the line on which BC lies, ∠ADB = 90°. Also, since AD = BD = 4, triangle ABD is an isosceles right triangle, so ∠ABD = 45°. Since C and D are both on the same horizontal ray from B to the right, ∠ABC = ∠ABD = 45°. Therefore cos B = cos 45° = √2/2.

method.method_draft: Use an auxiliary right triangle. From the image, note that BC is drawn horizontally along a grid line, and A is above and to the right of B. Drop a perpendicular from A to the line containing BC, meeting it at D. Count grid squares in the figure: the vertical distance AD equals the horizontal distance BD (the standard solution counts both as 4 grid units). Thus triangle ABD is a right isosceles triangle, so the angle between BA and the horizontal ray BD is 45 degrees. Since ray BC lies on the same horizontal line from B as BD, angle ABC is also 45 degrees. Therefore compute cos B = cos 45 degrees = sqrt(2)/2.
